subject: general
question: Which of the following metals is less reactive than silver ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Au**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The likelihood of metals to **donate electrons reduces **as we **down **the **reactivity scale**.
 
• Therefore, the **least reactive **metals are at the **bottom **of the series, and the **most reactive **metals are at the **top**.
 
• **Silver **comes **before gold **in the reactive series.
 
• **Silver (Ag) **is more reactive than** gold (Au).**
 
• The outer electrons of gold have the structure **5d10 6s1.**
 
• Its **5d **electrons are thus fully occupied, meaning it **lacks **readily available d electrons or orbitals for reacting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• As we proceed from **top to bottom**, both reactivity and the metals' reducing nature continue to get stronger.
 
• This indicates that the **strongest reducing agents **are the metals at the top of the reactivity series.
 
• As we travel from the bottom of the series to the top, the **electropositive character **of the elements likewise gets stronger.
 
• Metals positioned on the higher side also have a propensity to **corrode **or **tarnish **quickly.
 
• All **metals **in the series **above hydrogen **release **hydrogen gas **when they come into **contact **with either** diluted hydrochloric acid **or **diluted sulfuric acid. **
